prompts.prompt: Scan the Python files in C:/data/projects/skills/playwright/scripts for security vulnerabilities. Use the security-audit and secrets rulesets. Summarize findings by severity and tell me if any high-severity issues were found.
assertions: Uses scan_code tool with the target path and specified rulesets (p/security-audit, p/secrets)
Uses parse_findings tool to categorize results by severity level
Reports structured summary with high/medium/low counts and pass/fail status
Does not fall back to manual grep or regex-based ad-hoc scanning

with_skill.plan: 1. Call scan_code(target_path='C:/data/projects/skills/playwright/scripts', rules=['p/security-audit', 'p/secrets']). 2. Pass results to parse_findings() to get categorized severity breakdown. 3. Report the summary dict: high/medium/low counts, total findings, and pass/fail status based on whether any high-severity findings exist.

baseline.plan: 1. No scan_code or parse_findings tools available. 2. Attempt to run 'semgrep' via bash if installed, constructing CLI flags manually (semgrep --config p/security-audit --config p/secrets <path>). 3. Parse raw JSON/text output manually with no structured severity categorization tool. 4. Likely falls back to grep-based pattern matching for common issues (hardcoded passwords, eval usage) if semgrep is not installed, which is ad-hoc and incomplete.

prompts.prompt: List all available Semgrep rulesets I can use, then scan C:/data/projects/skills/github-actions/scripts using the OWASP Top 10 ruleset specifically. Tell me the total number of findings.
assertions: Uses get_available_rulesets tool to list available Semgrep rulesets
Uses scan_code tool with p/owasp-top-ten ruleset on the specified path
Uses parse_findings to extract total finding count from results
Reports the total_findings number from the parsed output

with_skill.plan: 1. Call get_available_rulesets() to list all available rulesets with descriptions. 2. Call scan_code(target_path='C:/data/projects/skills/github-actions/scripts', rules=['p/owasp-top-ten']). 3. Call parse_findings() on the results. 4. Report the total_findings count and list of available rulesets.

baseline.plan: 1. No get_available_rulesets tool. Would have to search Semgrep docs or run 'semgrep --help' to discover rulesets. 2. Could run semgrep CLI directly if installed: 'semgrep --config p/owasp-top-ten <path>'. 3. Would parse raw CLI output manually. 4. Could count findings from raw output but without structured parse_findings tool.

prompts.prompt: Run a security scan on C:/data/projects/skills/semgrep/scripts using the Python-specific ruleset. If the scan takes too long, make sure it times out after 60 seconds. Show me each individual finding with its file, line number, and severity.
assertions: Uses scan_code tool with p/python ruleset
Passes a custom timeout value of 60 to scan_code
Uses parse_findings to get the structured findings list with file/line/severity details
Reports individual finding details (not just summary counts)

with_skill.plan: 1. Call scan_code(target_path='C:/data/projects/skills/semgrep/scripts', rules=['p/python'], timeout=60). 2. Call parse_findings() to get structured output. 3. Iterate through the 'findings' list in the parsed result and report each finding's file path, line number, and severity level.

baseline.plan: 1. Could run 'semgrep --config p/python --timeout 60 <path>' via bash if installed. 2. The timeout flag maps directly to CLI usage. 3. Would parse raw text/JSON output manually to extract file, line, severity. 4. Can display individual findings from raw output but without structured parsing.
